target.title: feat(android): record and send voice notes from the chat composer
target.body:
Related: #100709 (iOS counterpart: #100946)

## What Problem This Solves

Android users have no way to send a quick, fire-and-forget voice message to their agent from the chat composer. Voice turns and Talk mode are live, synchronous interactions; neither covers "record 30 seconds now, get an answer whenever it's ready." Channels such as Telegram and WhatsApp already accept voice notes and transcribe them through media understanding — only the first-party app lacked a way to produce one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds tap-to-record voice notes to both Android chat composers (main chat screen and chat sheet), reusing the existing `chat.send` attachment path end to end. A `VoiceNoteRecorderController` state machine drives a fake-able `MediaRecorder` AAC/m4a mono engine (44.1 kHz, 32 kbps); one monotonic controller timer owns the named 3-minute cap and the single `stop()` path because Android's max-duration callback races its asynchronous recorder stop. The finished note is staged as a regular pending attachment (`audio/mp4`, named byte bound) and sent with the normal send button.

Two contract details matter. First, the MPEG-4 container's `ftyp` major brand is normalized to `M4A ` because the gateway sniffs attachment bytes with `file-type`, which classifies Android's default `mp42` brand as `video/mp4` and would route the note to video understanding instead of audio transcription. Second, recording participates in `NodeRuntime` microphone ownership: manual mic, Talk, and gateway PTT cannot acquire the microphone concurrently, and background/composition teardown cancels the recorder and removes its temporary file. The controller retains file ownership through asynchronous staging so cancellation cannot orphan a recording in the cache. `RECORD_AUDIO` permission is requested lazily on first use. No server changes: gateway `chat.send` already accepts non-image attachments and the reply pipeline transcribes audio via media understanding. Non-goals per the tracking issue: playback of sent notes, waveform visualization, slide-to-cancel, and offline queueing of attachments (attachments stay online-only per the outbox contract).

## User Impact

Android users can tap the mic button next to the attachment control in either composer, record up to 3 minutes with a live timer, cancel or finish, see the note as a "Voice note · m:ss" chip (optionally alongside text), and send it. Sent bubbles render a voice-note row with duration, preserved across the optimistic-echo → history reconciliation. If the gateway is offline, the existing attachments-online-only refusal applies unchanged.

## Evidence

- Fresh Blacksmith Testbox proof after rebasing over Android multi-gateway: `pnpm android:test`, `pnpm android:lint`, and `pnpm android:assemble` all `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` on Testbox `tbx_01kwwnep0p0h3j0r4j7zm3whg9`.
- Recorder regressions cover lifecycle/elapsed time, the controller-owned duration cap and single-stop invariant, oversize rejection, M4A brand normalization, mic mutual exclusion, permission denial, and cancellation/failure cleanup through `Preparing`. Gateway PTT rejection, outgoing payload/local-echo duration, history parsing, and duration reconciliation are also covered.
- Fresh autoreview after the overlapping multi-gateway rebase: clean, no actionable findings. Native i18n inventory and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Source-blind APK inspection with Android `aapt` confirms `uses-permission: android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO`.
- Real microphone capture/send remains manual-device proof; Android documents that `MediaRecorder` does not work on the emulator. Automated evidence does not claim this physical-device interaction.
